column7: Scope note: Core AI has no compiling first-party samples, so verify every signature in this part before trusting it.
ANE-authored model quietly runs on GPU: the coreai-models loader infers compute unit from entrypoint names.
Debug gauge appears only with direct CoreAI linking; via a package there is no row, reading as if the model never ran.
Omit remove_functionalization and KV writes vanish: fluent, globally incoherent output that mimics bad quantization.
Evidence note: no Apple samples or doc updates exist for this framework; claims rest on repos, headers and community.
enable_per_channel_scale=True makes rank-6 tensors that silently push the model off the ANE; it runs and burns battery.
A surviving nn.Linear converts fine but becomes a segmentation point, splitting the graph off the Neural Engine.
A mismatched projection transpose exports cleanly and yields structurally shuffled activations with PSNR in the teens.
Apple's skill file recommends einsum SDPA; the shipped iOS code uses per-head permute plus matmul instead.
Causal mask shaped (1,q,1,k) instead of (1,k,1,q) runs without error but collapses SDPA PSNR to 15-30 dB.
An M-RoPE that misses the exact cat([cos,cos]) then ::2 indexing pattern converts fine and outputs ~18 dB PSNR.
Caching new_k instead of key_rope stores pre-RoPE keys; shapes are identical but PSNR collapses to ~20 dB.
GELU substituted for SiLU runs like the original and is 20-30 dB off; activation functions are not interchangeable.
Odd mask dtype/shape or GQA combo makes PyTorch's dispatcher pick the math backend; the fused SDPA quietly decomposes.
from_source_model appears only in skill files; shipped coreai-models uses task-specific factories like from_hf.
A non-contiguous tensor through the Python wrapper can produce wrong numbers rather than an error.
Name entrypoints encode_image/encode_text/predict and the loader classifies your ANE model .dynamic, requesting the GPU.
The WWDC session's segmentation caching story does not match what the shipped CoreAISegmentationEngine does.
CoreAISegmentationEngine re-runs image_encode on every call; the session's 76% caching win needs your own orchestration.
CLI --n-bits/--group-size hit both encoders uniformly, silently overriding the recipe's asymmetric per-encoder settings.
The 76% second-inference figure omits device and warm-up protocol, and the shipped engine lacks the caching it assumes.
Zero Apple sample projects exist for Core AI; the strongest evidence is shipped repos, then headers, then community.
TOC pointer to the coreai-torch 0.4.0 IR-location incident and its provenance.
A package that links CoreAI links it for itself; your app shows no Debug gauge row and no warning explains the absence.
More-menu hand-off items only cover events recorded after the report page opened; earlier repros silently lack them.
Load and Specialization colours swap between Debug gauge and Core AI instrument, so colour intuition misreads traces.
An in-place mutation of a forward() input becomes hidden converted-model state; there is no flag to opt out.
trimKVCache returns -1 whenever extraStates is non-empty, so SSM and hybrid models silently re-prefill every turn.
Changing SpecializationOptions makes a second cache entry, doubling storage and cost; any OS update flushes the cache.
Never run an iOS-compiled bundle on a Mac: it can wedge the GPU/ANE stack into a watchdog reboot (community-reported).
The Core AI Debugger's paired-device list omits visionOS, tvOS and watchOS; whether it attaches there is an open gap.
TorchConverter's API doc shows a bare constructor and never mentions the real mode parameter.
A RELEASE-converted asset opens as a seemingly working Debugger session; the Source Viewer is just absent, unexplained.
AIProgram.optimize() can delete broadcasting-significant axis ops; the graph shrinks and the numbers go wrong silently.
Similarity metrics are per-forward-pass; they cannot certify a decoding loop.
An all-green sync-point board can coexist with different generated text: per-step errors compound in the decode loop.
The talk recommends EAGER for weight compression; the repo's recommended default is GRAPH - each fits different jobs.
Compression succeeds while log-only skips leave layers untouched; the asset is less compressed than you configured.
Short type keys like torch.nn.Linear silently match nothing; the config is accepted and the layer is quantized anyway.
Talk says 4-bit with per-channel scales on both encoders; the shipped recipe is asymmetric w4/gs32, w6/gs8 without.
Graph-mode op names are global, eager-mode are module-qualified; a pattern from the wrong mode matches no layers at all.
The only benchmarker test upstream is skipped; use benchmark numbers for ranking modules, not for publishing latency.
Per-module timings from benchmark_coreai_program are directional only.
Provenance of the incident that made every coreai-torch 0.4.0-converted asset permanently unusable.
Every .aimodel converted with coreai-torch 0.4.0 is dead: a wrong IR location breaks compilation (community, issue #37).
Inside the 0.4.0 incident: tooling reads the broken asset fine, making it look recoverable when it is not.
coreai-build inspect parses a 0.4.0-dead asset perfectly; every recovery attempt fails, each costing someone a day.
Audit dead assets by the missing producer field, but .aimodelc bundles always carry one, so use another field for those.
Intermediate filenames are community-reported; the audit script depends only on Apple-named metadata.json.
Apple maintainer fix for the 0.4.0 compiler failure: strip_debug_info, then save the updated asset.
The maintainer's snippet assigns strip_debug_info's return value, but it returns None; use the statement form.
Working pins: coreai-torch 0.4.1+, torch 2.9.0; letting uv bump torch to 2.11 breaks torchvision, killing every export.
Scope note: signatures in this guide come from shipped repos and community evidence, not Apple samples.
Pipeline diagram: omit remove_functionalization and KV writes vanish silently.
Pipeline diagram: after AOT compiling you must hand-edit the assets map in metadata.json.
The most common first mistake: pointing a runner at the inner .aimodel when it wants the bundle directory.
The .missingAsset error text doubles as fix instructions; read it before debugging.
Community audit counts 21 export recipes vs this guide's table; likely timing - run --list rather than trusting either.
coreai.llm.eval is declared in project.scripts but unconditionally errors with 'Evaluation support is coming soon'.
Registry compression presets reference YAMLs that exist only in the source tree; wheel installs exit with SystemExit.
get_c4 imports undeclared datasets and tqdm; activation quantization raises ImportError with an install hint.
input_names/state_names order is load-bearing: swap key and value and the model loads, runs, and emits fluent nonsense.
macOS wants keyCache/valueCache, iOS wants key_cache/value_cache; copying a name across targets fails at load, loudly.
The coreai-models auto-detect loader crashes on segmenter or speech assets instead of throwing a usable error.
nn.functional.silu lowers to cast+swish+cast the ANE cannot run; the graph partitions onto GPU/CPU with no diagnostic.
Model output buffers are only valid inside the async with block; call .numpy() before the context exits.
cpu_only() exists for numeric parity checks only; community measured ~9x slower than default() on a DiT.
AIModel.load(path, None) trips MPSGraph errors, and a GC'd AIModel makes the load_function return garbage, not a crash.
Without two env vars set at export, the Debugger's navigator has no debug metadata to show.
load_intermediates validates the directory suffix and raises if you point it anywhere else.
Bundles missing chat_template.jinja silently fall back to raw completion; quality collapses and nothing warns.
module_type_configs keys must be full internal paths; short names silently match no modules.
Compression completes while quietly skipping layers; the shipped asset is bigger and less quantized than configured.
Apple's two compression claims measure different things; they are not in conflict - keep baselines straight.
enable_per_channel_scale=True can push the model off the Neural Engine, per Apple's own shipped config comment.
This contradicts WWDC26 325:241's 'with per-channel scales'; the shipped code sets it False and wins.
The shipped macOS LLM preset uses eager mode, so it cannot use KV-cache quantization; graph mode is required.
Recipe line: remove_functionalization is mandatory - omit it and KV writes disappear (see 8.4).
Omit remove_functionalization and the KV cache never updates: fluent, incoherent output that mimics bad quantization.
remove_functionalization imports private coreai._compiler dialect modules; pin versions, it can break any release.
Breaking change vs pre-release code: input_names now also covers state names; older export scripts mis-bind.
optimize() deletes ops it deems dead, including broadcasting-significant axis manipulations; outputs change silently.
optimize() can hang outright on very large attention graphs.
An unknown model id ships an asset whose metadata has only creation_date; the banner warning scrolls past in long logs.
Skip chat_template.jinja in the bundle and runners fall back to raw completion; output quality quietly collapses.
inspect still reads the 0.4.0-dead asset fine, which makes it look recoverable; it is not.
'Won't open' hides two gates: the runtime load gate is OS-side, the authoring parse gate is in the wheel.
Running python from the coreai-torch clone shadows 0.4.1 with 0.4.0 egg-info; exports silently use the broken version.
coreai-build is not in the Xcode 27.0 beta app bundle — it ships in the Metal Toolchain component (resolved 2026-07-31); CI without that component sees only the aimodelc stub.
AOT arch strings track device identifiers, not marketing names; a name-matched guess produces an asset that won't load.
coreai-build compile exits 0 for any requested architecture; only a device load validates the choice.
A compile that exits 0 and an asset that loads on device are different claims; validate by loading.
AOT is no memory cure: a 1.8 GB ANE monolith loads on iPhone 17 Pro, then the first inference step is jetsam-killed.
expectFrequentReshapes=true on an all-static graph abandons the AOT specialization and segfaults with no error string.
Compiling with --expect-frequent-reshapes does not make the runtime hint safe; both variants crash - load-time matters.
An uncompiled .aimodel will not run on iOS at all; only the compiled .aimodelc loads there.
.aimodel dirs embedded in an app bundle fail as 'invalid bundle', and a root Resources/ folder breaks code signing.
Community rule: never execute an iOS-compiled bundle on a Mac - it can cost a watchdog reboot, not an afternoon.
The package pins mlc-ai/xgrammar to branch main, not a version; resolve and commit your own revision.
KV strategy .chunked is accepted by the API and does nothing.
.fixedSize pre-allocates the KV cache at full maxContextLength; short sessions pay the whole context's memory.
The 'growing strategy' error tells you to re-export with --dynamic-sized-kvcache-gpu, a flag no shipped CLI has.
The fastest engine throws on guided generation: @Generable needs per-step logits the pipelined path never exposes.
The pipelined engine also lacks forcedContinuation, so MMLU-style continuation scoring is impossible on it.
Mistral tool-call detection synthesizes a newline close marker; a multi-line [TOOL_CALLS] array breaks the parser.
swift run builds Debug by default; benchmark from a Release build or your numbers measure the wrong thing.
Only an LLM benchmark tool exists in the repo; no latency or quality numbers are published for non-LLM models.
ModelBundle.verify() runs only in the llm-runner CLI, not in init; a broken assets map surfaces later, in your app.
Checklist: KV cache is in-graph mutable state - remove_functionalization is what keeps its writes alive.
Checklist: never execute an iOS-compiled bundle on a Mac.
The fork snapshots an older upstream; commit 04a3fd6 upstream already stops pipelined generation when the stream drops.
COREAI_CHUNK_THRESHOLD is a memory dial and Apple's hint points the wrong way on a high-RAM Mac.
A second hidden knob: --bucket-size maps to COREAI_QUERY_BUCKET_SIZE; zero disables it.
Correction: MLX does run on iPhone GPUs via mlx-swift; only the ANE is closed, and FM integration is not exclusive.
mlx2coreai is a community MIT project at v0.1.1 with 11 commits, not Apple tooling; it vendors one Apple BSD file.
position_ids must be the full 0..total-1 vector every call, not just new positions, or RoPE indexing silently breaks.
coreai-models moved six commits past the pin; VLM bundles lost the .llmasset extension and the KV-cache primitives were rewritten.
Session 325:241's 'per-channel scales' conflicts with the shipped recipe; the shipped code wins.
